drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 76-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 1.43, creatinine 0.78, hemoglobin 14.4, lactate 1.9-3.2, platelets 130, sodium 140, wbc 17.9; vitals dbp 47-59, heart_rate 102-119, map 62-74, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 21-25, sbp 90-107, spo2 96-97, temp 38.5-38.9
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Blood cultures x2; Lactated Ringer's 30 mL/kg IV bolus; Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.75, hemoglobin 14.3, platelets 133, sodium 140, wbc 14.3; vitals dbp 63-71, heart_rate 86-102, map 78-88, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 17-21, sbp 109-123, spo2 96-97, temp 37.2-38.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 76-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
